players.product: Advanced-packaging inspection/metrology (Dragonfly G5, 3DI) + JetStep panel-level lithography

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO, non-GAAP): record revenue of $267 million, a 22% increase from Q3; full-year revenue finished at $1.005 billion, also a record for Onto Innovation. Gross margin improved by about 50 basis points to 54.6%; operating margins improved to 25.2%, up 410 basis points from Q3; adjusted diluted EPS $1.26. CEO: orders from 2.5D packaging for AI devices more than doubled in the quarter, and Onto set a record for cash generation of $95 million (cash conversion of approximately 150% of non-GAAP net income).
quarterly_data.figure: record revenue $267 million (22% increase from Q3); full year $1.005 billion; gross margin 54.6%; operating margins 25.2%; adjusted diluted EPS $1.26; record cash generation $95 million

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (point-in-time): Q1 revenue of $275 million to $285 million as demand strengthens across advanced packaging and advanced nodes; Q2 revenue expected to surpass $300 million, giving 12% to 14% core growth in the first half of 2026 versus the second half of 2025. Backlog, customer confidence and the newly signed VPA lead management to expect higher revenue in the second half of 2026 than the first half, with margin expansion each quarter this year. Q1: approximately 50 basis points of gross margin improvement from Q4 (tariff mitigation, more shipments from extended factories), operating expenses of approximately $80 million (full quarter of Semilab costs), operating margins of approximately 25.5% to 26.5%, EPS of $1.26 to $1.36. From Q1 Onto moves to calendar quarters with fiscal year-end December 31.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $275 million to $285 million; Q2 revenue to surpass $300 million; 12% to 14% core growth in the first half of 2026 vs the second half of 2025; Q1 operating margins 25.5% to 26.5%; Q1 EPS $1.26 to $1.36

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging grew over 25% sequentially in Q4, driven by Dragonfly inspection, Iris films metrology and established 2.5D applications; sales from the 2.5D packaging business doubled versus Q3. Advanced packaging and specialty devices were approximately $145 million in Q4 (slightly more than half of revenue, including approximately $9 million from Semilab) and $504 million for 2025. 2026 outlook: advanced packaging revenue to grow over 30%, a new record ('It's OSATs, it's panel. It's all of advanced packaging.'), and 'relatively stable' between the first half and second half; the guide assumes no large Dragonfly G5 adoption ('We've taken a conservative approach there'), so G5 could add second-half upside. CEO: 'the vast majority of that 30% growth is all tied to supporting the strong demand in AI'; Onto no longer splits out AI packaging because many OSATs and specialty packaging customers are joining that supply chain. CoWoS and HBM inspection growth in 2026 is expected to be relatively similar (CoWoS has higher capital intensity); G5 wins could swing it toward CoWoS.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging and specialty devices approximately $145 million in Q4, $504 million for 2025; advanced packaging to grow over 30% in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Next-generation inspection: Onto is supporting 4 separate customer evaluations of its next-generation inspection systems (the G5, which the analyst described as Onto's 'new high-resolution Dragonfly platform') at customers' facilities. Preliminary feedback is positive, citing significant improvement in optical performance and higher throughput. The qualifications target 2.5D packaging and high-bandwidth memory, including next-generation hybrid bonding, where current-generation tools are already used for process control and R&D. The timeline is unchanged: 'accelerated evaluations to end in the Q1, Q2, the first half of the year with hopefully starting to catch ramps in the second half of the year.' 3D metrology is becoming more crucial for die stacking and fan-out, and the 3Di metrology pipeline is expanding beyond HBM. Semilab's surface charge metrology, which addresses residual charge on die in large-format heterogeneous packaging, received its first orders.
quarterly_data.figure: 4 separate customer evaluations of next-generation inspection systems; evaluations to end in the first half of the year

quarterly_data.signal: Panel-level packaging: Onto won orders in the quarter for JetStep and 8 Firefly systems to support 'an exciting new large panel packaging facility'. The orders are 'the first of several potential phases of expansion', and the panel customer serves AI applications. Multiple advanced-packaging customers placed further 3Di purchase orders, including an OEM that needs precise metrology for new panel-level process development. Customers are adopting Firefly process control in glass and panel fan-out, feeding metrology into the stepper for shot-by-shot adjustments, and JetStep prints large packages without stitching. In lithography, after a period of heavy industry overcapacity, customers are 'beginning to resume orders'. Onto expects this to increase into 2027, and the data suggests 2027 'will be in supply-demand where there's just not enough supply to meet the demand'. CEO: end customers such as 'the AMDs, et cetera, are looking for alternatives' to traditional advanced packaging so they can scale.
quarterly_data.figure: orders for JetStep and 8 Firefly systems for a new large panel packaging facility

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and supply: Onto is set up to serve a $2 billion run rate, and that has 'only improved as we bring up the extended factories', with a transition period over the next couple of quarters while those factories ramp. On constraints: 'I don't see capacity being a big issue for us. It's more on the supply chain side'. Fast order growth and customer pull-ins are straining suppliers, 'especially in the area of precision optics', where lead times are relatively fixed, and Onto is working with customers and suppliers to manage 'tightening capacity and the gradual extension of lead times'. Backlog nearly doubled over the last 3 months to a record of approximately 2 quarters, and several customers' forecasts now extend into 2027. More than 50% of tools were delivered from the extended factories in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity for a $2 billion run rate; backlog nearly doubled over the last 3 months to approximately 2 quarters; more than 50% of tools delivered from extended factories in Q4

players.product: HBM inspection & metrology (Dragonfly G5 2D inspection, 3D metrology, 3Di sub-surface) + Atlas G6 OCD for DRAM

quarterly_data.signal: Onto announced a volume purchase agreement with one of its HBM customers (not named) covering Dragonfly 2D and 3D bump metrology demand through 2027. The agreement is valued at over $240 million, including over $60 million in systems for 3D bump metrology. In Q&A, management said it is a 2-year agreement that was 'more 2027 weighted, so maybe 2/3, 1/3', but demand is accelerating and 'we're starting to see this move towards this 50-50 kind of a range'. It mainly covers current products already qualified for the customer's 'aggressive ramp' ('So it's G3s now'), with upgrade options offered. Onto expects additional VPAs and is in discussions with other customers. CEO: 'Memory is definitely expanding, and we have a good position in memory.'
quarterly_data.figure: VPA valued at over $240 million, including over $60 million in systems for 3D bump metrology; through 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Front-end memory metrology: the recently announced Atlas G6 is being adopted for new critical applications in both gate-all-around and HBM4 DRAM, which management expects to add to growth in 2026. DRAM spending timing falls in the second half of the year.

players.product: Advanced-node process control: Atlas G6 OCD transistor metrology (<2nm), Iris films, integrated metrology

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced nodes revenue more than doubled in 2025 to $308 million. The growth came from DRAM and logic (together about 75% of the total) and Onto's strong OCD position at leading global logic and memory manufacturers, with less than 3% of revenue from China. In Q4, advanced nodes grew slightly over 30% sequentially to $72 million, mainly on pilot-line sales to a new gate-all-around customer. Films metrology and integrated metrology both set revenue records in 2025. Integrated metrology is expanding beyond memory to 2 logic customers for leading-edge processes expected to ramp in 2026. Demand is 'really all driven by gate-all-around'; at 5-nanometer and above, the attach rate for OCD 'was much less'.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced nodes 2025 revenue $308 million (more than doubled); Q4 $72 million (slightly over 30% sequentially); DRAM and logic about 75%; less than 3% of revenue from China

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 advanced-nodes outlook (point-in-time), measured against the 10% to 20% WFE growth analysts project: 'I would expect us to at least perform in that range of the 10% to 20%, so 15% plus in that range for advanced nodes'. The CFO put it at 'probably somewhere mid-teens as those orders kind of firm up'. Demand is broad, with customers asking how quickly Onto can support their ramps, but timing is uncertain: several factories are expected to open, DRAM timing is in the second half, and several customer discussions tied to purchase agreements could refine the number. New products (HSIR, Atlas G6, 3D) are early penetrations at 'maybe 10% of the business, maybe a little less' this year. They are growing into 2027 and opening new applications that expand Onto's SAM.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced nodes 2026 growth 15% plus (at least in the 10% to 20% WFE growth range); new products maybe 10% of the business

quarterly_data.signal: The Semilab acquisition closed on November 17: Onto paid $445 million in cash and issued 641,771 shares. Semilab contributed about $9 million of Q4 revenue after the mid-November close. 2026 Semilab revenue was initially framed at 'somewhere low $100 million to $110 million', but power semi, a significant portion of Semilab's business, may be more challenged in 2026 than first thought as Onto pivots Semilab from opportunistic sales to longer-term opportunities. Power semiconductor revenue was strong in Q4 but is expected to decline seasonally in Q1, and to decline around 10% in 2026 on weakening EV demand and slowing infrastructure spending.
quarterly_data.figure: Semilab: $445 million in cash and 641,771 shares; about $9 million Q4 revenue; 2026 low $100 million to $110 million; power semi revenue to decline around 10% in 2026
